Do you like to challenge and are you fluent in Norwegian and/or Swedish and have a profound understanding for the Norwegian market?
- Then you could be the one we are looking for to join our Norwegian sales department at Nordiccom!

Nordiccom is a Danish company located in Copenhagen and we are still growing. Our Norwegian team is working hard and would love some new energetic colleagues joining them on our sales team, who’s responsible for selling insurance solutions to existing customers in the financial sector. All sales are made over the phone.

We are looking for a characteristic person with a flair for working with people over the phone and making sure the customers get a great experience every time. The position is on site from our office in Copenhagen and we only have contact with our customers over the phone.

It is not a requirement for you to have experience with insurances prior to applying for this job, but we would prefer it if you have experience with selling over the phone. 

Qualities we highly value from you:
- An energetic personality with a “can do”-attitude, who knows how to smile through the phone
- Confidence and the ability to work as part of a team
- Good communication skills and the ability to connect with all kinds of different people
- A competitive and result-oriented mindset
- Fluent in Norwegian (English language skills are also an advantage)
- Huge plus if you have experience working with tele sales/telemarketing from a previous job

What you can expect from us:
- Guaranteed wage combined with attractive bonus & commission agreements and prizes
- A social working place in a comfortable & productive environment
- A multinational working environment with an informal tone and high job satisfaction
- Helpful and motivated colleagues
- Advantageous working hours and traffic connections near Copenhagen city.
- Office located in the heart of Copenhagen

You don't need to have experience with insurances or experience working with the financial sector to apply for this job.
It is important to us that our employees deliver the highest quality of service, which is why we provide thorough training, ensuring that you are ready to meet any challenges and deliver good results while feeling comfortable in your new role.

Who are we and what do we do?
Nordiccom ApS is a growing Nordic company located in the heart of Copenhagen and Helsinki. The companies we represent are major banking and insurance companies in Europe. With the entire Northern Europe market as our workplace, and the phone as our tool, we provide solutions for sales and customer service for a wide range of companies in the financial business. Therefore, we comply with the banks’ standards and code of conduct, so quality is ensured. In Nordiccom you will meet both Danes, Norwegians, Finns and Swedes. Nordiccom consists of about 150 employees divided into different teams. In Nordiccom, we emphasize professionalism, and it is important that we thrive when we are at work. Our goal is that we shape our employees for success. That they become skilled at their work and achieve good results. All training is practiced in your own language.

If this sounds interesting to you, please don't hesitate to send your resumé and an application marked "Norwegian sales agent".

The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  The project 
 The position is centred on the development of integrated superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) embedded in controllable photonic circuits for the fully integrated processing of the emitted photons from silicon quantum emitters. The work will be performed as part of the Photonic Control and Readout team in NQCP, in close collaboration with the Theory & Simulation and the Materials engineering teams at NQCP and the Growth team at Quantum Foundry. These teams will support the efforts of the development and integration of SNSPDs in our photonic circuit.

  You will be collaborating closely with the other team members of the Photonic C&R team and – like the rest of the team - be generally involved in the projects related to the platform. A number of students will also be dedicated to the SNSPD projects. The nanofabrication is done at the DTU Nanolab – a 1,350 m² ISO 4–6 cleanroom with over 150 state-of-the-art tools, and one of the leading cleanrooms in Europe. Testing and integration of the SNSPDs will be done at the NQCP Photonics lab at the Niels Bohr Institute established in 2023. The lab contains a range of cryostats (mK to 4K) designed for optical fibre access, state-of-the-art electronics, commercial SNSPDs, etc.

  Responsibilities:

   	
• Taking the leading role in developing and integrating SNSPDs into our photonic circuits and establishing the electrical control circuit. 	
• Structuring the efforts on multiple projects, integrating experimental results in our database, and providing feedback to collaborating teams. 	
• Contributing to the other projects within the Photonics team. The projects span single photon sources and optical components like switches, cavities, etc. 	
• Teaching and supervision of students. 	
• Procurement, maintenance, and operation of scientific equipment.    

  We are looking for the following qualifications: 

   	
• PhD with postdoc experience in experimental physics, engineering, nanotechnologies, or related. 	
• Experience with SNSPDs fabrication and characterisation, quantum photonics, electronics, and cryogenic systems. 	
• Experience with control software and data logging – preferably in python. 	
• Good communication skills and a structured approach to work.   
 Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.
 
 The position is also open as a postdoc. Please apply to the call corresponding to the position relevant for you. Only one of the positions will be filled.

As Advanced Regulatory Writer, you will help get Novo’s manufacturing processes approved and keep them approved. You will write and manage the product registration documentation that regulators rely on, and help shape the regulatory storyline with project teams across the product lifecycle. Your clear, accurate submissions keep products moving through approval, so treatments can reach the people who need them without avoidable delay.

What you’ll bring

• An MSc in Life Sciences, Pharmacy or a related field.

• 2+ years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, for example in manufacturing support, clinical or regulatory writing, or Regulatory Affairs.

• Demonstrated knowledge of, or experience with, API regulatory documentation, product registration and compliance with regulatory requirements.

• Strong technical writing skills: you produce clear, concise and complete regulatory documents, and some API process knowledge.

• Meticulous attention to detail, so documents are accurate and complete and submissions are not delayed.

• The ability to manage several regulatory tasks at once, keep to timelines and adapt when priorities change.

• Clear communication of regulatory requirements to stakeholders, and an easy way of working across functions.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience taking part in audits or authority inspections, or in process optimisation and regulatory improvement projects.

What you’ll do

You will be the link between regulatory requirements and the people who make our products. Your work helps approvals and changes move forward with clarity.

• Prepare, update and review regulatory submission documents so they meet the requirements of regulatory agencies.

• Answer questions from health authorities.

• Work with Regulatory Affairs, the project manager and process development teams to support the approval and maintenance of drug manufacturing process registrations.

• Advise on manufacturing changes to make sure they comply with regulations.

• Represent regulatory writing in project teams throughout the product lifecycle: give input to the regulatory storyline and to project plans, including timelines for preparing and approving submission documents.

• Share learnings, changes and authority signals with the department, and contribute ideas for regulatory strategies that speed up approval of product and manufacturing process changes.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the API MSAT Project Office, working as the regulatory writing representative in project teams. You will be able to work independently on most tasks, with guidance from more experienced colleagues when you need it.

Your closest internal partners are API MSAT, API manufacturing, CMC development (all including QA), Regulatory Affairs, Global Contract Manufacturing (GCM) and Material MSAT, including primary packaging. Externally, you will work with contract manufacturing organisations (CMOs).

The role is based at the Bagsværd site, with the option to work from Gentofte and Kalundborg. Bringing different expertise together, and speaking up early when timelines or documents are at risk, is how this team moves quickly and gets to a clear decision.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to own your documents and your voice will count in project teams. You will join cross-organisational networks, project, process and focus groups, and contribute to regulatory optimisation projects. That gives you the chance to broaden your regulatory expertise and build new skills across the value chain, with the support of experienced colleagues.

As Filling Professional, you will help keep aseptic production on stable and compliant. Working side by side with operators on the shop floor, you will support daily production, apply systematic problem solving and improve how the line runs. Your work helps high-quality treatments reach people living with serious chronic diseases, and you will learn aseptic production from a holistic perspective.

What you’ll bring

You are comfortable in a hands-on GMP production environment and enjoy working directly with the people who run the line. You bring:

• A Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Biology, Pharmacy, Biotechnology, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related scientific or technical field.

• Fluency in Danish and English.

• Experience from a GMP-regulated production environment, ideally within pharmaceutical manufacturing.

• A systematic and solution-oriented approach to problem solving, with the ability to support production issues and drive them towards resolution.

• A proactive and collaborative mindset, with the confidence to work closely with operators and take ownership of tasks.

• An improvement-minded approach, with an interest in LEAN principles and continuous improvement.

Useful, but not essential

• Hands-on process support experience, working closely with operators and production teams.

• Familiarity with GMP documentation, including deviation and change cases.

• Experience with continuous improvement or Lean.

What you’ll do

You will be part of the process support team around aseptic filling, helping production run safely, compliantly and with continuous improvement in mind.

• Give proactive daily support to production through board meetings, handover meetings and regular shop-floor presence.

• Explore production and process challenges together with operators, using systematic problem solving.

• Work in accordance with current GMP requirements and support high standards of quality and compliance throughout production.

• Make sure batch documentation from filling and Vial Packer (VPA) follows the release flow, and support batch review.

• Write and update Standard Operating Procedures and work on deviation and change cases.

• Contribute to continuous improvement that makes the line more efficient and reliable.

Who you’ll work with

You will join Filling Line 11 Process Support, a team of around 18 colleagues with diverse backgrounds. The team is part of Drug Product Manufacturing in Kalundborg, where approximately 520 colleagues turn Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients into finished products for people all over the world, from formulation and filling to visual inspection.

Your closest partners will be the operators and the other professionals who support the line. Clear communication, honest feedback and speaking up early keep the work moving smoothly.

jobs.occupation: Product Marketing Manager - B2B Software for Manufacturers
jobs.description:
Highlights:

• Fast-growing B2B software platform with established global reach is looking for our first marketing hire.

• We have a broad, multi-product offering for a narrow industry, and we don't fit into a single existing "category box" as defined today -- giving you a meaty challenge to work with.

• We have large customers and touch a lot of users (as a platform for managing global supply-chains), so your work will be "heard around the world"

• We are a small, efficient, get-stuff-done team. Looking for someone who things that's the way to go.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality — with a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth. We have done very little marketing.

That is where you come in.

The role

This is our first marketing hire.

You will own positioning, messaging and sales enablement for a platform that already has real customers, real reference stories and real competitive wins — but no one whose job it is to articulate any of it. There is no existing playbook to inherit, no legacy brand guidelines to work around, and no committee to navigate. There is a large amount of low-hanging fruit and a clear runway to make a visible commercial impact within your first few months.

You will work directly and closely with our co-founder and CEO, who continues to run product. He knows the product and the domain deeply; what he needs is a strong product marketing partner to turn that into sharp positioning, messaging that lands with procurement, quality and operations buyers, and material that makes the sales conversation easier.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You will be writing the copy, building the deck and updating the website — not briefing an agency to do it.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and in this role in particular, the close working relationship with management & sales is much easier to build in person.

What you will do

• Own positioning and messaging for the Supplios platform and its individual modules, and make it consistent across every touchpoint

• Translate technical capability into buyer-relevant value for distinct personas — sourcing and procurement leads, supplier quality engineers, quality directors, supply chain and operations management

• Build the sales enablement layer: pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, demo narratives, proposal content and objection handling

• Run competitive and market intelligence, and keep the team honest about where we genuinely win and where we do not

• Plan and execute go-to-market for new modules and major releases, in step with the product roadmap

• Develop customer proof — case studies, reference stories and use cases — from an installed base that has plenty to say

• Rebuild our website messaging and product pages so they reflect what we actually do and who we do it for

• Feed structured market and customer insight back into product decisions

What we are looking for

Essential

• Proven product marketing experience in B2B or enterprise software, with responsibility for positioning, messaging and sales enablement

• A demonstrable track record of translating complex, technical products into clear commercial value propositions

• Excellent written English

• Comfort operating without a marketing team, an established playbook or a large budget — you scope the work, then do it

• The temperament for a small, senior, fast-moving company: high ownership, low ceremony

Nice to have

• Domain knowledge in automotive, industrial manufacturing or supply chain. Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. We can teach the domain to the right marketer; we cannot teach product marketing to a domain expert.

• Experience marketing to enterprise buyers with long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

• Experience as an early marketing hire at a growing B2B software company

Language

• English is the only important language for this position — we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• First marketing hire, not the fifth. You define how this company talks about itself.

• A product that already works. Real global customers in a demanding vertical, and reference stories waiting to be told.

• Work directly with the CEO/founders. No layers between you and the decisions.

• Visible impact. In a company that has barely marketed, good product marketing shows up in the pipeline quickly.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Predictive Human Digital Twins for Human-Centred Systems Engineering – DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Are you interested in human-centred engineering at the intersection of biomechanics, artificial intelligence, and systems engineering, and want to build a strong methodological profile, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity – including the chance to help shape a new research group from the start.

At DTU Construct, you will develop methods that turn generic musculoskeletal models into personalised Human Digital Twins – based on sparse wearable sensor data instead of costly laboratory measurements or medical imaging – and assess how reliably they predict how a person moves and interacts with technical systems such as collaborative robots or assistive devices. The project is part of building up a new research group in Human-Centred Design within the Human-Centred Systems Engineering activities at DTU Construct. As part of the DTU PhD programme, you will follow PhD-level courses and contribute to teaching.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall purpose will be to develop and validate methods for personalising biomechanical Human Digital Twins from sparse sensor data, combining physics-based and data-driven approaches and quantifying the gap between simulation and reality (sim2real).

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Develop methods for personalising musculoskeletal models from sparse multimodal sensor data.
• Combine physics-based and data-driven approaches for model calibration and prediction.
• Quantify and reduce the sim2real gap of Human Digital Twins.
• Plan and carry out experimental studies with human participants.
• Implement your methods in open, reusable software.
• Publish your results and collaborate with researchers at DTU and international partners.
We are looking for a motivated candidate with:

• An MSc in Biomedical or Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering Design, or a related field.
• Solid programming skills (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++).
• A background in simulation, optimisation, machine learning, sensor processing, or parameter estimation.
• A strong interest in computational modelling of humans and human-technology systems.
• Good communication skills in English and the ability to work both independently and in a team.
• Experience with musculoskeletal modelling (e.g. OpenSim, AnyBody, SCONE), motion analysis, or wearable sensing is an advantage.
• We do not expect you to master all of these areas – a solid foundation and the motivation to grow into the field matter most.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

The Section of Engineering Design and Manufacturing Systems (EDM) advances the design of intelligent, resilient, and sustainable products and manufacturing systems, integrating systems engineering, modular architectures, robust and bio-inspired design, and AI-enabled engineering.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. jobs.occupation: Senior Contract and Warranty Manager – Hobro, Denmark
jobs.description:
Do you have experience in managing complex operations contracts and commercial risk across countries? Do you enjoy building something into the next level?

We are looking for a Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to take end-to-end ownership of operations contracts across Eurowind Energy's global wind, solar and BESS portfolio.

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to join our Global Operations team. Based at our Operations office in Hobro, you will be the contract and warranty specialist for our global asset portfolio, supporting colleagues and managers across countries and functions.

Your role

As Senior Contract and Warranty Manager, you will take ownership of key commercial agreements, claims and warranty matters across Eurowind Energy's global asset portfolio. You will work closely with Asset Management, Operations, Finance, Legal and local teams to ensure that our contractual rights are understood, protected and actively used. The role combines hands-on contract management with a strong focus on risk, value creation and standardization across markets.

• Own contract management for operations contracts, including service and O&M agreements, warranty and performance guarantees, grid connection and curtailment compensation, insurance, land lease and supplier agreements

• Lead negotiation, drafting and execution of contracts so they meet both legal and commercial requirements

• Identify, assess and mitigate commercial and legal risk across the contract portfolio

• Manage claims and warranty follow-up, making sure issues are tracked, escalated and resolved in line with contractual terms

• Build global contract templates, playbooks and governance processes that work consistently across countries

• Monitor contract performance and compliance, flagging risks and improvement opportunities

• Be the go-to contact for the country teams and the wider operations organisation on contract questions and disputes

You will work with the country operations teams, Strategic Commercial Management (which owns PPAs, power trading and balancing contracts), Technical Operations, Investor Administration, SCADA Operations, Legal, Finance, and suppliers and service providers. Your role is to strengthen the countries' ability to manage contracts locally, not to add another layer of bureaucracy.

What we offer

You will join Global Operations at a time where we are transforming how we manage and operate our global asset portfolio. You will get a broad international scope, close collaboration across functions and countries, and the opportunity to work with complex commercial and operational challenges. We offer a high level of autonomy, a strong professional environment and the opportunity to make a visible impact on how Eurowind operates.

• A newly created role where you set the structures and ways of working

• The chance to make a real impact on how we improve and operate our commercial mindset

• Ownership, trust and room to shape your own area

• A global role with some travel, in an international and energetic environment

• A workplace in Hobro, alongside our operations colleagues

You will join a newly established team and report to Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management. Louise is a collaborative and pragmatic leader who builds strong relationships, creates alignment across functions and empowers people to take ownership. She combines a deep understanding of the organisation with a practical focus on execution and a global perspective.

Required competencies and skills

You have solid experience with contract management, commercial agreements, warranties and/or claims, ideally from the energy, infrastructure, construction or other asset-intensive industries. You are comfortable navigating complex contractual matters and working across technical, commercial and legal topics. You combine strong analytical and negotiation skills with a pragmatic approach and the ability to turn contractual knowledge into action and business value.

• Significant experience in contract management within energy, infrastructure, renewables or another asset-intensive industry

• A proven record of leading complex contract negotiations end-to-end, including service and O&M, warranty, grid/curtailment, insurance and supplier contracts

• Solid understanding of commercial and legal risk management, with experience building or applying compliance frameworks

• Relevant legal, commercial or technical education (for example law, business or engineering), or equivalent hands-on experience

• International experience and comfort working across countries and cultures

• Enjoys building something new and setting up structures from scratch

• Works autonomously across a global organisation and values being part of a team

• Structured and detail-oriented, yet pragmatic about getting things done without unnecessary process

• Communicates clearly and directly, holding suppliers and internal stakeholders accountable while working with respect

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn

Did we capture your attention?

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below. As we continuously review incoming applications, please send us your CV as soon as possible.

Should you have any questions before applying, please feel free to contact Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management, at lth@ewe.dk.

Do you want to help protect critical energy infrastructure at the heart of the green transition? Are you energised by working directly with local businesses across Europe, understanding their challenges and mobilising the right expertise to solve them?

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Global Cyber Security Consultant to join our team in Hobro, Denmark.

As an operator of critical energy infrastructure, cybersecurity is a vital part of how we protect our business, our partners and the communities we serve. As Eurowind continues to grow and adapt to an evolving threat landscape and regulatory requirements such as NIS2, we are strengthening security as an integrated part of the organisation – in every market where we operate.

You will join our Group Cyber and Information Security team – a small, senior team supporting a global organisation, anchored directly with the CISO. Cyber and information security is delivered centrally from Group headquarters to all our markets, and we do not scale through headcount alone, but through expertise, smart automation and AI. That means real ownership, meaningful responsibility and the opportunity to shape how security is delivered across Eurowind.

Your role

This is a new and highly visible role. As Group Cyber Security Advisor, you are Group Cyber and Information Security’s face in our 14 markets. You build trusted relationships with country management and site teams – remotely and, when it adds value, on site – and uncover where they need help within cyber and information security – from regulatory compliance and supplier risk to securing operational technology at our energy parks.

You will not solve everything yourself, and you are not expected to. Behind you stands the full Group organisation: security operations, architecture, GRC and legal specialists who deliver the concrete solutions. Your job is to identify the need, activate the right expertise at headquarters, and support the local organisation through implementation – so our markets get consistent, high-quality security support from within the Group instead of relying on external consultants.

Your work will include:

• Acting as the primary point of contact for cyber and information security in our local markets and building strong relationships with country management

• Conducting structured assessments of local needs, risks and maturity – across IT, OT and compliance – using a common Group framework

• Translating local needs into concrete deliveries from Group specialists in security operations, GRC, legal and architecture

• Supporting local implementation of Group security initiatives, standards and controls, including NIS2, ISO 27001 and IEC 62443 requirements

• Making our markets aware of the security services already available to them through the Group, reducing the need for external advisors

• Reporting findings, progress and risks back to the CISO and contributing to Group-level prioritisation

What we offer

We believe security starts with understanding the business: what needs protecting, why it matters and how security can help the organisation move faster and more safely. That is exactly what this role embodies – security delivered in partnership with the business, not imposed on it.

Our role is not to block progress, but to help Eurowind operate securely and confidently globally, under NIS2 and in an increasingly demanding threat landscape.

We also believe good security starts with strong fundamentals. It is easy to chase the cutting edge, but most organisations are exposed because the basics are not consistently in place. For us, that means strong visibility, reliable detection and well-practised response – consistently, in every market. We do not dismiss bold ideas – we build the foundation that makes them viable.

Just as importantly, we believe better security comes from building a better team. We value people who challenge assumptions, think independently and bring different perspectives. Leadership in our team is about creating the conditions for better answers to emerge, not pretending to have all the answers.

In return, you will get:

• A unique, self-directed role with international reach and direct impact across 14 countries

• Direct anchoring with the CISO and close collaboration with senior stakeholders across the Group

• A strong specialist backline – you are the front figure, never alone with the problem

• Access to modern AI tools and automation to amplify your impact

• Pension and health insurance

• Flexible working hours and a hybrid working model based at our headquarters in Hobro – with the opportunity to travel to our European markets when it makes a difference

Required competencies and skills

This role is less about deep technical specialisation and more about judgement, communication and drive. You are comfortable walking into a country office or an energy park and earning trust quickly – whether you are talking to a country manager, a site technician or a local lawyer. You can hold a conversation about regulatory obligations in the morning and OT security at a substation in the afternoon, and you know when to bring in a specialist.

We imagine you bring:

• Solid experience within cyber and information security, for example from consulting, advisory or a broad security role in an international organisation

• A working understanding of regulatory frameworks such as NIS2, and ideally exposure to OT/industrial environments or IEC 62443

• Strong stakeholder management skills and the credibility to engage with local management

• A structured and analytical way of working – you turn conversations into clear assessments and actionable requests

• The confidence to work independently across borders while knowing when to pull in the backline

• Excellent communication skills in English; additional European languages are an advantage

• Willingness to travel occasionally across our 14 markets

It’s a plus if you have:

• Experience from the energy sector or other critical infrastructure

• Experience working in a Group/HQ function delivering services to local entities

• Hands-on experience with security assessments, gap analyses or audit-style engagements

• Used AI or LLMs as practical tools in your workflow

This is a new and highly visible role. As Group Emergency Preparedness Advisor, you own that Eurowind is ready before a crisis happens – not that you personally run the response when one occurs. You make sure our global emergency preparedness has the plans it needs, that those plans are kept current and fit for purpose across all markets, and that the people who will use them are trained and confident enough to act.

Just as importantly, we believe better preparedness comes from building a better team. We value people who challenge assumptions, think independently and bring different perspectives. jobs.description:
Job Description

• 
Job ID: 369138

• 
Date posted: 26/10/2026

Who you are

We're looking for an experienced Retail Interior Design and Visual merchandising Specialist, who can inspire and surprise our customers by presenting and communicating the IKEA home furnishing offer through inspirational, functional, and aesthetic range presentations and can share our home furnishing knowledge by contributing and participating in events and activities, workshops, Instagram, Live shopping etc.

• You have a high passion for creating inspiring store solutions for an easy and convenient shopping experience and increasing vitality by translating deep knowledge about consumer buying behavior, store layout, range presentation, and local market knowledge.

• You are innovative, dare to challenge yourself and always want to improve and learn.

• You are easy to adapt to changes and able to act quickly to exploit commercial opportunities.

• You have a high visual competence with a keen eye for aesthetics, ability to draw, visualize and present an idea.

• Computer proficient with knowledge and experience of using relevant software e.g. Revit

To succeed in this assignment, you will contribute to togetherness; build strong relationships, collaborate, and co-create with your many colleagues with your creative mindset. You can make things happen with flexibility, speed, and simplicity.

Your responsibilities

• Work hands-on on the shop floor and use your retail design & visual merchandising competence to strengthen the uniqueness of the IKEA identity in range presentation solutions by working with the store layout, range presentation, and vitality.

• Actively contributing to gathering insight about store layout and range presentation and translating this knowledge into relevant and inspiring store solutions that will support a convenient shopping experience and reflect the local needs in life at home.

• Secure high quality, simplicity, efficiency, and cost consciousness in planning and implementing all range presentations by applying national and global tools and best practices.

• Secure vitality and seasonality in the store by contributing and implementing the commercial calender.

Our team within IKEA

You will become part of a strong team in our Home Furnishing & Retail Design function, consisting of graphic designers, interior designers, visual merchandisers, and leaders. While others see furniture, we see smart home furnishing solutions that can create a better everyday life for many people. With passion and imagination, we transform colors, textiles, and furniture into inspiring environments that surprise and convince our customers. We work closely with other departments every day, giving you experience in collaborating with many different people. We are an international team with a strong sense of unity, where we support each other and work together. There is therefore room to be exactly who you are. We provide the right training so you can feel confident and competent in the job. At IKEA, you have endless opportunities for development.

Apply now!

Instead of a traditional cover letter, we'd love to get to know you through a short video application. Please upload your video as an MP4 file (maximum 3-5 minutes).

Please introduce yourself and answer the following questions:

• What interests you most about this role?

• What makes you a strong candidate for this position, and why?

• How would your best friend describe you in three words, and why?

No need for professional equipment or editing. Just be yourself - we're looking forward to getting to know the person behind the CV.

If you have questions or inquiries, you're welcome to contact Retail Solution Manager Nadine Hinterseer via nadine.hinterseer3@ingka.ikea.com.

Please notice that we do not receive applications via e-mail but only through our recruitment portal.

Further information

• The position is 37 hours per week on average

• You will primarily work within the hours of 08:00AM - 16:00PM Monday to Friday. Evening and weekend work may occur

• We offer various employee benefits, including a pension plan, health insurance, massage program, canteen, employee discount, discount agreements with partners, annual gift etc.

• Preferred start date is December 1st 2026.

• Please note that relocation support, including assistance with relocation-related documentation, is not included in this position.

Like homes, talent is also diverse, and in IKEA we have a passion for real people. We would love to get to know you as there is a wide range of opportunities in IKEA, based on desire, ability, and experience. We hope you will join us on this adventure and we are looking forward to hearing from you.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to accelerate high-quality biomarker testing so the right patients receive the right treatment, faster? As a Diagnostic and Scientific Liaison, you will be the in-country scientific expert who turns strategy into practical testing solutions that directly impact patient identification and care in your assigned Nordic country. the testing landscape so clinicians have the evidence they need when it matters most?

Our AstraZeneca Nordic Marketing Company employs around 550 people and has offices located in Copenhagen, Stockholm, Oslo, and Espoo. AstraZeneca Nordic is a recognized leader in its core therapy areas and aims to improve the lives of millions of people. This is an area where you are free to be more – you are encouraged to challenge traditional ways and test your curiosity. We drive innovative science, deliver key launches, build close collaboration and partnerships within health care.

You will build trusted partnerships with laboratory leaders, pathologists, molecular specialists, and oncologists, bringing scientific clarity and technical guidance to every interaction. Working cross-functionally, you will translate Nordic and global diagnostic direction into focused country plans, remove barriers to timely testing, and help ensure robust, reliable diagnostics are available across the patient journey.

Accountabilities:

• 
Shape Diagnostic Strategy: Assess the country’s diagnostic landscape, patient pathways and laboratory capacity, translating insights into practical testing plans aligned with Nordic and global priorities.

• 
Build Scientific Partnerships: Engage laboratory leaders and scientific experts related to the brands and their diagnostic challenge through trusted relationships, education and tailored technical communication.

• 
Drive Brand science in context to the diagnostic strategy. Work holistically with the scientific experts ensuring they buy fully in to the science behind the in line or future brands and the need for diagnosing the right target segment.

• 
Improve Testing Quality and Access: Identify barriers and bottlenecks, champion quality and appropriate testing, and co-create compliant solutions that improve timeliness and equity.

• 
Generate Insights and Evidence: Provide diagnostic intelligence to support launches, tactical planning, validation, real-world evidence, and research initiatives.

• 
Lead Cross-Functional Projects: Drive priorities from planning to delivery, collaborating across country, Nordic and global teams to improve consistency, quality and efficiency.

• 
Uphold Governance and Compliance: Ensure all activities meet the highest scientific, ethical, privacy, safety, quality and compliance standards, escalating risks appropriately.

Essential Skills/Experience:

• 
Relevant Background: Degree in life sciences, biomedical science, medicine, pharmacy or a related field, with approximately 3–5 years’ experience in diagnostics, biomarker testing, clinical laboratories or healthcare.

• 
Diagnostic Expertise: Working knowledge of diagnostic pathways, laboratory operations and testing methodologies, with confidence interpreting scientific and technical data.

• 
Communication and Influence: Ability to explain complex science clearly, deliver compelling technical presentations, and build trusted external relationships.

• 
Project Delivery: Strong planning, prioritisation and stakeholder-management skills, with a track record of delivering projects in matrix organisations.

• 
Language and Mobility: Fluency in English and the relevant local Nordic language, with willingness to travel regularly in-country and across the Nordics as needed.

• 
Valid driver’s license as this is a field-based role.

Desirable Skills and Experience

• 
Advanced Expertise: Advanced degree or experience in oncology diagnostics, companion diagnostics or biomarker testing, including IHC, NGS or PCR.

• 
Industry Experience: Background in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics or clinical laboratory environments.

• 
Quality and Regulatory Knowledge: Understanding of local diagnostic regulations and quality-assurance requirements.

• 
Stakeholder and Launch Experience: Experience partnering with laboratories, healthcare professionals and diagnostic providers, and supporting launches, testing implementation, validation, research or real-world evidence initiatives.

• 
Nordic Collaboration: Experience contributing to cross-country or Nordic projects.

Inclusion & Diversity

We are proud to have a unique workplace culture that inspires innovation and collaboration! Here, employees are empowered to express diverse perspectives - and are made to feel valued, energized and rewarded for their ideas and creativity.

Why AstraZeneca

Join a team where science leads decisions, and collaboration turns evidence into real change for people living with cancer. Here, unexpected teams gather around the same table to unleash bold thinking, fusing medical expertise with strategic execution to change clinical practice. You will work at the forefront of diagnostics, partnering with external experts and cross-functional colleagues to shape every point in the patient journey. We back ambition with support, value kindness alongside high standards, and create space to test new ideas, learn quickly and scale what works—so your contribution reaches patients, not just slide decks.

So, what is next?

Step into this pivotal role to elevate precision diagnostics in your country and help transform cancer care - bring your scientific credibility and project leadership to where they’ll make the biggest impact today.

Welcome with your application, in English, latest by the 15th of November 2026!

Applications will be reviewed continuously throughout the application period.

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora.
